test_title: RRB NTPC CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 2 Feb 2021 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: From where have the words 'Satyameva Jayate' which are inscribed below the National Emblem of India, been taken?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Mundaka Upanishads**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The words **Satyameva Jayate **from **Mundaka Upanishad**. 
 
• The **saying **of the **Indian National Emblem **is **'Satyamev Jayate' **or '**Truth Alone Triumphs.**
 
• It is **written **in the **Devanagari script**.
 
• The **word alludes **to an **antiquated Sanskrit Vedic content**, which is **inserted inside Atharva Veda**.
 
• It had **been embraced **as **the public aphorism **of **India **on the **date of 26 January 1950**.
 
• It is **engraved **in the **Devanagari script **at the foundation of the **Lion Capital of Ashoka **and furthermore frames a basic piece of the Indian public seal. 
 
• The image and the words "**Satyameva Jayate" **have been **engraved **on more than one side of **all Indian money just **as the **public records**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Puranas **are **religious texts **composed in **Sanskrit**, orally narrated for **centuries **before being **written down from the 2nd century CE **onwards. They are **part of the sacred literature **of the Hindu faith that **also comprises **the **Vedas**, **Brahmanas**, **Aranyakas**, **Upanishads**, and the **great epics**.
 
• **Bhagavadgita **is an **episode recorded **in the **great Sanskrit poem of the Hindus**, the **Mahabharata**. It occupies chapters **23 to 40 of Book VI **of the **Mahabharata **and is **composed **in the form of a **dialogue between Prince Arjuna and Krishna**, an avatar (incarnation) of the **god Vishnu**.
 
• **The Jatakas **are a **voluminous body **of **literature **native to **South Asia **which mainly concern the previous births **of Gautama Buddha **in both **human **and **animal form**. According **to Peter Skilling**, this genre is **"one of the oldest classes of Buddhist literature**."
